extracted.intended_audience: general public, donors, corporate and policy partners, and prospective supporters
extracted.subtask_description: An organizational landing/about page describing Environmental Defense Fund's mission, methods, partnerships, and examples of past work to persuade and inform the public and potential partners/donors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding practical, powerful, nonpartisan solutions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as EDF's core mission; illustrated by historical examples such as leading the resurgence of the bald eagle and removing lead from gasoline to protect children's health. Serves as a high-level criterion for EDF projects: they should be practical, powerful in impact, and nonpartisan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation, efficiency and common sense
rubrics_metrics.description: "Innovation, efficiency and common sense continue to be EDF watchwords in the 21st century."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should emphasize innovative approaches, efficient use of resources, and pragmatic common-sense solutions. Page cites development of solutions across a wide range of contemporary challenges as examples of these principles in action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships with leading companies
rubrics_metrics.description: "Partnerships with leading companies — from FedEx to McDonald’s to Walmart — have saved companies and consumers money, reduced packaging and other waste, accelerated innovation and made everyday products safer for families."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDF prioritizes collaboration with private-sector partners to achieve environmental goals that also create business value; examples given include corporate partners and outcomes (cost savings, reduced waste, safer products).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipartisan creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bipartisan Creativity" (EDF economists helped the first Bush administration develop measures that saved hundreds of thousands of lives by giving power plant owners flexibility to use lower-sulfur coal ... delivered a return on investment of more than 30 to 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDF highlights working across party lines and using creative policy designs that balance environmental benefits with economic and political feasibility; success measured in lives saved and high ROI, and includes a presidential commendation quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scientific methods and evidence ('Scientists in action')
rubrics_metrics.description: "Scientists in action" — e.g., pioneering high-resolution health risk detection using Google Street View cars, advising on chemical safety legislation, organizing oil and gas research partnerships to locate, measure and repair wasteful leaks of natural gas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDF projects are expected to be science-driven: develop and apply technical methods, conduct large-scale collaborative research, and use data to identify and fix environmental problems. Specific examples show methodological innovation (neighborhood-level detection, satellite and vehicle-based measurement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollution reduction through industry agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "brought together BP, ExxonMobil, Shell and dozens of other companies in an agreement to reduce some of the most harmful pollution from oil and gas production by as much as 90%."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor negotiated, industry-wide agreements that achieve large percentage reductions in harmful pollution; success measured by the scale of reduction and breadth of participating companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical remediation programs (e.g., gas well capping)
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "helped create programs for oil and gas workers to safely cap and seal wells no longer in production that had been leaking pollution."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational, on-the-ground programs that enable workers to remediate pollution sources safely and effectively are a criterion for EDF interventions; emphasis on practical implementation and worker involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land conservation through partnerships with landowners
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "partnered with ranchers, farmers and other landowners to enable innovative conservation actions on more than 5 million acres of working lands."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservation strategies should work with private landowners to implement innovative, voluntary actions at scale; success measured by acreage enrolled and collaborative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of commercial resources via policy and industry collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "worked with policymakers, grocery stores and commercial fishing groups to restore profitable fishing in coastal Texas and Louisiana after the Deepwater Horizon disaster, with restoration measures backed by large bipartisan margins in the U.S. House and Senate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that restore natural-resource-based livelihoods (e.g., fisheries) are expected to combine scientific backing, policy action, and industry/stakeholder buy-in; political support and profitability are cited as success metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improving food supplies through corporate and technological partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "partnered with Danone, General Mills, Kraft Heinz and other major food companies to increase sustainability of dairy products," worked with farmers and agribusiness to improve fertilizer efficiency, and developed satellite-based analysis of agricultural water use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approaches that improve agricultural sustainability via industry partnerships, efficiency improvements, and data/technology (satellite analysis) are emphasized; outcomes include reduced costs, improved ecosystems, and better farm management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value creation via environmental performance measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: EDF "teamed up with KKR and The Carlyle Group to make measuring, managing and improving environmental performance a core part of value creation across the private equity industry."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding environmental metrics into investment and value-creation frameworks is a criterion: environmental improvements should be quantifiable and tied to economic value for investors and companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on measurable impact and supporter engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section headings and CTAs ('By the numbers', donation matching, 'Join a powerful force of over 3.5 million allies') emphasize measurable impact and mobilizing public support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EDF frames success in measurable terms (members, partnerships, acres conserved) and prioritizes clear calls to action for donors and supporters as part of its outreach and impact strategy.
